headline: Coalition Says It Intercepted Houthi Missiles Bound for Riyadh
deck: Saudi civil defence lifted a Riyadh aerial-threat alert after two explosions were heard in the capital.
body: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthis towards Riyadh early on Saturday, after emergency alerts in the Saudi capital [E1][E8]. It said the missiles were destroyed [E8][E13]. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki announced the interceptions shortly after 2 a.m., after a Riyadh alert warned residents of an aerial threat [E9].

Two explosions were heard in Riyadh, witnesses said, after which civil defence lifted the alert and said the danger had passed [E10]. The Houthis said they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh [E11]. Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on Riyadh after vowing reprisals for a coalition special operation [E12].

The attack came two days after a Houthi strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower, the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper [E2]. Saudi Arabia had issued and quickly lifted Riyadh alerts for a third consecutive day [E3]. Its civil defence agency issued eight public emergency alerts during the 24 hours beginning at 7:30 a.m. Saudi time on Friday [E4].

Turki al-Malki said coalition strikes hit operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles [E5]. The Houthis threatened attacks on Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports and warned airlines that Saudi airspace was unsafe [E6].
The United Nations said it was following the escalation with concern [E7].
